## The two failures, and what they mean

### 19 · App resources — `Wide310x150Logo.png` wrong size — **fixed**

> `Image reference "assets\Wide310x150Logo.png": The image "assets\Wide310x150Logo.png" failed the
size restrictions of 310 X 150.`

Real bug: no wide tile art was ever generated, so the manifest pointed at a file that either did
not exist or was square. Fixed in `scripts/generate-icons.cjs` — it now writes
`Wide310x150Logo.png` (310×150), `Square310x310Logo.png`, `Square71x71Logo.png`, `SmallTile.png`
and `LargeTile.png`, drawing the mark scaled to fit instead of stretched. Verified inside the
rebuilt package: all eight assets have exactly the required pixel sizes.

### 25 · Blocked executables — Electron's own code — **cannot be fixed, not a blocker**

> `File app\PC Wrapped.exe contains a reference to a "Launch Process" related API kernel32.dll!CreateProcessW`
> `File d3dcompiler_47.dll contains a blocked executable reference to "reg"` / `"cmd"` / …

Every Electron app trips this: the runtime can spawn processes, and the bundled
`d3dcompiler_47.dll` contains strings that look like executable names. WACK marks the test
`OPTIONAL="TRUE"`, and this is exactly how it is supposed to be for a Win32 (Centennial) app. PC
Wrapped genuinely does launch one process — `powershell.exe` running `tracker.ps1` — which is the
tracker, by design.

## What this does and does not prove

It proves the package is structurally valid, correctly signed, uses no debug configuration,
declares the right capabilities, and passes the manifest and UAC checks. It does **not** replace
the Store's own review, and it does not test the app while running. That is still worth doing
once from the installed package.
